abbQuestion: Which pod causes the CPU spike?

requiredMembers: victim CFS throttled-period ratio > 0.25 default bar (T0, on the edge-inference container)
node /proc/pressure/cpu some-stall > 0.10 default bar (T0+, one runs-on hop away on vigil-worker2)
expectFindings.span: pod -> vigil-worker2 over a valid runs-on edge
expectFindings.why: the edge-inference container (100m limit, full-speed loop) throttles ~90% of CFS periods while the telemetry-burst pods drive node-wide PSI; the conjunction is a FULL match anchored on the victim.

attribution.method: MEASURED blast radius + runs-on topology (the loud co-located CPU consumer on the victim's node)
attribution.note: Attribution is via the AUTHORED match structure (required victim throttle + required node PSI) plus MEASURED topology, NOT a learned blame score and NOT generated text.

dropConditions.why: the PSI member becomes observable-and-not-met, failing the conjunction; throttling without node pressure is not the cascade. Vigil must stop firing on the victim once node pressure clears.

mustNotFabricate.statement: Vigil must NOT pick the culprit pod via a learned/model blame weight or a generated reason. The 'which pod' answer comes only from MEASURED topology (runs-on) + the deterministic match.
mustNotFabricate.charter: No learned edge/weight/threshold; reasons are only human-authored graph notes.

mustNotFabricate.statement: Co-location on the node is a MEASURED runs-on fact, not a proof that telemetry-burst CAUSED the throttle. Vigil surfaces the topology and the conjunction; it must NOT assert a fused causal claim beyond the AUTHORED cascade structure it matched.

note: The operator's 'which pod causes the spike' is answered by the deterministic match + runs-on topology pointing at telemetry-burst as the node-pressure source — never by a learned culprit-picker.
